newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Naphtha premium disappears.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Naphtha premium disappears.

text.p: Singapore naphtha remained bearish with the premium on a fob barrels disappearing on Wednesday, traders said.
A U.S. major sold a full cargo of 240,000 barrels lifting first-half September, at par to Singapore fob quotes (with conversion).
Traders had assessed the premium at 30-40 cents per barrel in the absence of any trade. Just in the middle of July, Singapore August barrels had fetched as much as a $1.00 premium.
"There is a lot of naphtha around," said a trader.
The North Asian market was dominated by sellers with only one buyer heard, but which was soon to disappear, traders said.

Adding to the regional surplus, Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) issued a tender to sell 125,000-barrels of naphtha lifting September 8-9 from Colombo, a company official said, which closes August 13 and offers valid for two days.
Gasoline was dull with Tuesday's buyer absent, and no other talk on the fixed price market.
Traders were heard instead searching for cargoes for the U.S west coast.
"The arbitrage is huge," said one trader. "But there are no barrels that can meet the strict specs."
No results were heard yet on Petron's closed tender which closed Monday.
But some traders said it was likely to be awarded to a South Korean refiner who was in a position to supply all three products - gasoline, gas oil and jet - that Petron is seeking.
"If all three are co-loaded, the freight cost is less than 40 cents per barrel from Korea...it (the refiner) is in the strongest position to win," a South Korean trader said.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
